basis: Restrictive cardiomyopathy and valvular abnormalities define the disease; hepatomegaly and ascites do not establish direct hepatic damage.
Cardiomyopathy with defining ectodermal abnormalities; persistent hair abnormalities affect roughly 36-75%. Other organ damage is not established as common.
Drug-resistant mycobacterial infection predominantly affects the lungs; resistance does not establish additional organ involvement.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing ventricular arrhythmias; syncope and vertigo do not establish neurologic or vestibular damage.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; glaucoma and intellectual disability each annotated at 80-99%, ventricular septal defect at 30-79%.
Medication-induced movement disorder with impaired motor control and restlessness; no additional organ involvement is established.
Anticonvulsant toxicity primarily impairs CNS function, causing ataxia, nystagmus or depressed consciousness; severe cardiac toxicity is not consistently common.
Mood disorder falls within the explicit psychiatric exclusion; the description as a brain disorder does not establish a separate neurologic disease.
Renal tubular salt transport disorder defined by salt wasting and electrolyte abnormalities, including hypokalemia and hypochloremia.
Varicella infection with defining vesicular skin lesions; pulmonary and neurologic complications occur in a minority.
Congenital attachment of the tongue to the mouth floor; tongue and oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited epidermal fragility causing localized palmoplantar blistering, with nail abnormalities; no extracutaneous disease is established.
Cerebellar motor disorder with ataxia, developmental delay and cerebellar atrophy; nystagmus alone does not establish primary eye damage.
Nonsyndromic inherited intellectual disability; no additional organ involvement is established.
Warburg micro syndrome is defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment, ocular abnormalities and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; cataract and glaucoma affect nearly all.
Brain, cardiac and ocular malformations define the syndrome; genital malformations have no axis and do not alone establish endocrine dysfunction.
Cold-reactive autoantibodies cause immune destruction of red blood cells; peripheral cold symptoms do not establish common lasting vascular damage.
The spectrum explicitly encompasses myofibrillar myopathy, cataract and cardiomyopathy; their combination varies across subtypes.
The supplied definition specifies parasitic infection of striated muscle; toxin-associated gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish common direct intestinal damage.
External auditory canal atresia and middle ear abnormalities cause conductive hearing loss.
Histiocytic proliferation infiltrates lymph node sinuses; individual skin, bone, respiratory and CNS sites are not affected in at least 30%.
Broad congenital syndrome grouping with variable intellectual disability; no additional organ axis is consistently established across its diverse subtypes.
Functional disorder defined by impaired colonic function despite absence of an identifiable structural or biochemical lesion.
Toxic injury to the optic nerve, which belongs to the ocular axis; toxicity does not imply an autoimmune mechanism.
Follicular skin disease causing scar-like atrophy and eyebrow hair loss; eyebrow location does not establish ocular damage.
